"''And you, you're welcome back here anytime.|Ranzar Malk and Din Djarin|}} The '''Roost''' was a [[space station]] that served as the base of a crew of [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] led by [[Ranzar Malk]]. The [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] known as [[Din Djarin]] visited the space station to join a [[Ranzar Malk's crew|team]] of mercenaries, who had been tasked by Malk into [[Bothan-Five incident|rescuing]] the [[prisoner]] [[Qin]] from the ''[[Bothan-5]]'', a [[New Republic Correctional Transport]]. The team betrayed Djarin and left him for [[Death|dead]], but he escaped and returned to the station with Qin, the latter unknowingly carrying a [[Homing beacon|tracker]] from the prison ship. Malk paid Djarin and let him leave, but ordered a [[gunship]] to shoot him down. However, a [[New Republic]] [[Adelphi Rangers|X-wing squadron]] followed the tracker's [[distress signal]] and opened fire on the station when they detected the gunship, destroying it.{{Topps|set=2023 Topps Star Wars|cardname=Jib Dodger|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/370777/cid/22170344}} ==Description== The station had some shielding, but lacked weaponry, making it vulnerable to attack.''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]'' {{Station-stub}} ==Behind the scenes== The Roost first appeared in the [[Chapter 6: The Prisoner|sixth episode]] of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''. The space station was designed to reflect real-world automotive chop shops, where sweaty workers cut up and assemble motorcycles and hotrods in a greasy and spark-filled garage, as opposed to the makeshift [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel]] or orderly [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] hangars typically seen in ''[[Star Wars]]''. Concept supervisor [[Ryan Church]] shaped the space station's exterior to consciously reflect [[Cloud City]], but interpreted more crudely. For the chop shop's aperture to space, Church intentionally moved away from the parallel lines of Imperial or [[First Order]] hangars, choosing a trapezoidal design instead.{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-6-guide|text="The Prisoner" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} While the [[2025]] [[Star Systems of the Galaxy]] appendix included a [[Roost system]] in the Bitrose sector, the system in question refers instead to a separate [[Roost system/Legends|Roost system]] from [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]]. ==Appearances== *[[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian'' Junior Novel]] {{Ab|The Mandalorian Junior Novel (audiobook)}} *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 1|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 1]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}} {{1st}} *[[The Mandalorian 6|''The Mandalorian'' 6]] ===Non-canon appearances=== *''[[Disney Magic Kingdoms]]'' {{Imo}} ==Sources== {{ScrollBox| *{{SWYouTube|aOC8E8z_ifw|The Mandalorian | Official Trailer | Disney+ | Streaming Nov. 12|sw_url=video/the-mandalorian-official-trailer}} {{1stp}} *{{SWYouTube|2RVnrBLOBcI|The Mandalorian | Special Look | Disney+}} *{{DisneyGallery|Directing}} *{{DisneyGallery|Legacy}} *{{DisneyGallery|Cast}} *{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-stagecraft-feature|text=This is the Way: How Innovative Technology Immersed Us in the World of ''The Mandalorian''}} {{1stID|Roost}} *{{DisneyGallery|Technology}} *{{DisneyGallery|Connections}} *{{SWYouTube|kb2K2wPFVUQ|Season 1 Recap | The Mandalorian | Disney+|sw_url=video/season-1-recap-the-mandalorian}} *{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-6-guide|text="The Prisoner" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} *{{InsiderCite|198|Jedi Master's Quiz}} {{Po}} *[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]] *''[[The Mandalorian: Allies & Enemies]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian -
